prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Quick Desktop Controls", "Learn how to interact, hide, and summon your pet on your desktop anytime.", "Click pet to play, right-click menu to sleep or hide"]
1: ["Preparing desktop engine assets and syncing pet attributes..."]
2: ["For best results, upload clear photos with steady lighting and distinct pet features."]
3: ["Setup Complete", "Your desktop companion is configured and ready to inhabit your workspace.", "Launch Companion", "Ready for Desktop"]
4: ["Sign in with your original account email to automatically restore your previously saved pets."]
5: ["Official Pet Adoption Certificate", "Review and seal your pet companion certificate."]
6: ["Practice Pet Commands", "Try out basic mouse clicks and tray gestures to manage your companion on screen.", "Test Pet Summon"]
7: ["Select Your Adoption Journey", "Pick a ready-to-play starter pet or generate a unique custom companion from photos."]
8: ["Signing in secures your companion data across devices and enables cloud synchronization."]
9: []
